For each file, find EVERY string that can reach a player's screen, and report it in the structured output. That includes:
- chat/console messages: game.print, player.print, force.print, surface.print
- flying text (player.create_local_flying_text etc.)
- GUI: caption=, tooltip=, text= on LuaGuiElement .add{} or assignments, including strings inside localised-string tables
- commands.add_command name + help text, and every response string those commands print
- custom alerts, message dialogs, set_goal_description, chart/map tag names, anything else display-bound
- data-stage: localised_name/localised_description, prototype names/descriptions, setting prototypes
- error() messages and log() calls (classify as category 'error'/'log', visibility 'log-only' or 'debug' as appropriate)
- strings handed to other mods or external systems (remote interface return values that get displayed, Discord bridge payloads) → category 'external'

- hazards, any of: 'concat' (sentence built by concatenation), 'plural' (text hardcodes singular/plural like "1 slot"/"slots" or picks between them in Lua), 'sentence-fragments' (reusable fragment strings composed into sentences elsewhere), 'rich-text' (embeds [color=]/[item=]/[font=] tags), 'server-side-string' (built into a plain Lua string before display, so all players would get one language), 'discord-mirror' (also sent to Discord/external where a LocalisedString cannot go), 'symbol-only', 'sorted-by-text' (list sorted by the display string), 'newlines' (embedded \n layout).

files_scanned must list every file you read (repo-relative), even ones with zero strings. In notes, mention anything structurally interesting for the localisation plan (helper functions that build messages, message pipelines, patterns repeated across files).

Your final output is consumed by a script, not a human — return only the structured data.

2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Thin wrapper around player.gui.top that provides a shared top-bar button
6	-- strip and a central click-handler registry.  Every GUI module registers its
7	-- own button and handler here.
8	-- NOTE: mod_gui was removed in Factorio 2.x; we use player.gui.top directly.
9	
10	local nav = {}
11	
12	-- name → function(event) registry, populated at module load time via nav.on_click.
13	local handlers = {}
14	
15	-- The ordered button list lives in storage.nav_button_order (array of
16	-- { name, sprite, tooltip } in registration order), NOT a module-local: a peer
17	-- that loads a save whose gui.top already holds the buttons must compute the same
18	-- insert index as the host. A module-local reset to {} on that peer's load, so
19	-- position_after_mts returned a divergent index -> gui.top child order (a
20	-- checksummed part of MP state) differed across peers -> desync.
21	
22	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
23	-- Public API
24	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
25	
26	--- Add a sprite-button to the top GUI bar for this player.
27	--- Idempotent: safe to call on reconnect; skips creation if button exists.
28	--- spec = { name = string, sprite = string, tooltip = string }
29	function nav.add_top_button(player, spec)
30	    -- Record registration order in storage BEFORE the create guard, so a peer
31	    -- that early-returns (button already exists in a loaded save) still records
32	    -- the order. Called only from on_player_created / on_player_joined_game
33	    -- (event context), so the storage write is legal and deterministic.
34	    storage.nav_button_order = storage.nav_button_order or {}
35	    local known = false
36	    for _, s in ipairs(storage.nav_button_order) do
37	        if s.name == spec.name then known = true; break end
38	    end
39	    if not known then
40	        storage.nav_button_order[#storage.nav_button_order + 1] =
41	            { name = spec.name, sprite = spec.sprite, tooltip = spec.tooltip }
42	    end
43	
44	    local flow = player.gui.top
45	    if flow[spec.name] then return end
46	    local btn = flow.add({
47	        type    = "sprite-button",
48	        name    = spec.name,
49	        sprite  = spec.sprite,
50	        tooltip = spec.tooltip,
51	        style   = "tool_button",
52	    })
53	    btn.style.width  = 56
54	    btn.style.height = 56
55	end
56	
57	--- Register a click handler for a named GUI element.
58	--- Typically called once at module load time, not per-player.
59	function nav.on_click(name, fn)
60	    handlers[name] = fn
61	end
62	
63	--- Dispatch a gui_click event.  Returns true if the element name had a
64	--- registered handler and the event was consumed.
65	--- Call this as the first thing in control.lua's on_gui_click.
66	function nav.dispatch_click(event)
67	    local el = event.element
68	    if not (el and el.valid) then return false end
69	    local fn = handlers[el.name]
70	    if not fn then return false end
71	    local player = game.get_player(event.player_index)
72	    if not (player and player.valid) then return false end
73	    event.player = player
74	    fn(event)
75	    return true
76	end
77	
78	--- Recreate all registered nav buttons for a player from the stored order/specs.
79	--- The live reconnect path recreates buttons via register_nav_buttons -> each
80	--- module's add_top_button; this is a convenience to rebuild the whole strip.
81	function nav.rebuild_buttons(player)
82	    for _, spec in ipairs(storage.nav_button_order or {}) do
83	        nav.add_top_button(player, spec)
84	    end
85	end
86	
87	--- Find the 1-based index to insert a new button so it stays grouped with
88	--- the mts buttons (right after the last registered mts nav button).
89	--- Other mods' buttons are pushed after this group.
90	--- Returns nil if none of our buttons are present yet (caller should append).
91	function nav.position_after_mts(player)
92	    local top = player.gui.top
93	    -- Build a set of our button names for fast lookup (from the shared stored
94	    -- order, so this resolves identically on every peer).
95	    local mts_names = {}
96	    for _, spec in ipairs(storage.nav_button_order or {}) do mts_names[spec.name] = true end
97	
98	    local last_idx = nil
99	    for i, child in ipairs(top.children) do
100	        if mts_names[child.name] then
101	            last_idx = i
102	        end
103	    end
104	    if not last_idx then return nil end
105	    return last_idx + 1
106	end
107	
108	return nav

2	-- Author: bits-orio

4	--
5	-- An admin-editable info panel in the dead center of the landing pen. The host
6	-- edits its text from the Admin panel's "Run Info" tab to describe each run
7	-- (mods, goals, rules) so players landing in know what they're playing.
8	--
9	-- Built on the base-game display-panel entity (present with OR without Space
10	-- Age), pre-configured with the info icon and both visibility toggles, and left
11	-- NON-OPERABLE so it is display-only: clicking it opens nothing. All editing goes
12	-- through the Admin GUI via a script write, which sidesteps the pen's spectator
13	-- permission group (scripts/spectator/core.lua) -- that group blocks the
14	-- edit_display_panel_* input actions for everyone, admins included, so the native
15	-- panel GUI can't be used. Writing display_panel_text from a script needs no
16	-- input action, so no permission-group or force change is required.
17	--
18	-- Also charts the small pen area for every force, so the island + panel stay
19	-- visible on the map even for a player who spawned onto their team surface before
20	-- the pen finished charting (otherwise the pen reads as a black island when they
21	-- look back at it).
22	
23	local helpers = require("scripts.helpers")
24	
25	local pen_info_panel = {}
26	
27	local SURFACE_NAME = "landing-pen"
28	local PANEL_NAME   = "display-panel"
29	local PANEL_POS    = {x = 0, y = 0}            -- dead center of the pen island
30	local CHART_AREA   = {{-20, -20}, {20, 20}}    -- covers the whole radius-15 island
31	local DEFAULT_TEXT = "An admin can describe this run from the Admin panel (Run Info tab)."
32	
33	-- ─── Text ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
34	
35	function pen_info_panel.get_text()
36	    return storage.pen_info_text or DEFAULT_TEXT
37	end
38	
39	-- Push the stored text onto the live panel. The panel is in single-message mode
40	-- (no circuit conditions), so display_panel_text is writable; pcall-guarded so
41	-- an unexpected mode never crashes the caller.
42	local function apply_text(panel)
43	    if not (panel and panel.valid) then return end
44	    pcall(function() panel.display_panel_text = pen_info_panel.get_text() end)
45	end
46	
47	--- Set the run description (from the Admin GUI). Persists it and updates the live
48	--- panel if the pen already exists; otherwise ensure() applies it on pen build.
49	function pen_info_panel.set_text(text)
50	    storage.pen_info_text = (type(text) == "string" and text ~= "") and text or nil
51	    apply_text(storage.pen_info_panel)
52	end
53	
54	-- ─── Panel entity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
55	
56	-- Pre-configure so an admin only ever edits the text: info icon, always-show
57	-- (alt-mode) + show-in-chart on, indestructible + non-minable, and non-operable
58	-- so its (permission-blocked) native edit GUI never opens.
59	local function configure(panel)
60	    panel.destructible = false
61	    panel.minable      = false
62	    panel.operable     = false
63	    pcall(function()
64	        panel.display_panel_always_show   = true
65	        panel.display_panel_show_in_chart = true
66	        panel.display_panel_icon = {type = "virtual", name = "signal-info"}
67	    end)
68	    apply_text(panel)
69	end
70	
71	--- Ensure the info panel exists at the pen center and is configured. Idempotent.
72	--- No-op if the display-panel prototype is unavailable (e.g. a mod removed it).
73	function pen_info_panel.ensure(surface)
74	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then return end
75	    if not prototypes.entity[PANEL_NAME] then return end
76	
77	    local panel = storage.pen_info_panel
78	    if not (panel and panel.valid) then
79	        -- Reuse one already at the spot (e.g. after a reload dropped the ref).
80	        local found = surface.find_entities_filtered{name = PANEL_NAME, position = PANEL_POS, radius = 1}
81	        panel = found[1]
82	        if not (panel and panel.valid) then
83	            -- Owned by the same force pen players are on (spectator), so its text
84	            -- is visible to them; fall back to the player force if absent.
85	            local force = game.forces["spectator"] or game.forces.player
86	            panel = surface.create_entity{name = PANEL_NAME, position = PANEL_POS, force = force}
87	        end
88	        if not (panel and panel.valid) then return end
89	        storage.pen_info_panel = panel
90	    end
91	    configure(panel)
92	    return panel
93	end
94	
95	--- True if this is the pen info panel (so pen chunk-gen doesn't clear it).
96	function pen_info_panel.is_panel(entity)
97	    return entity and entity.valid and entity.name == PANEL_NAME
98	        and storage.pen_info_panel == entity
99	end
100	
101	-- ─── Charting (fix: pen reads as a black island when viewed from afar) ──
102	
103	--- Chart the pen area for one force so the island + panel are always visible.
104	function pen_info_panel.chart_for(force)
105	    if not (force and force.valid) then return end
106	    local surface = game.surfaces[SURFACE_NAME]
107	    if surface and surface.valid then force.chart(surface, CHART_AREA) end
108	end
109	
110	--- Chart the pen for every force (called once when the pen is first built).
111	function pen_info_panel.chart_all()
112	    for _, force in pairs(game.forces) do
113	        pen_info_panel.chart_for(force)
114	    end
115	end
116	
117	return pen_info_panel

1	-- gui/platform_hub.lua
2	-- Anchors mod-registered widgets into the native space-platform-hub GUI via a
3	-- relative GUI. Mirrors the custom team-tab system: a mod registers a widget
4	-- (remote_api.register_platform_hub_widget) and fills the frame it is handed
5	-- through the on_platform_hub_gui_built event, raised each time a player opens
6	-- a platform hub. The frame is rebuilt every open so its content can reflect
7	-- the specific hub (entity.surface.platform / its location).
8	
9	local remote_api = require("scripts.remote_api")
10	
11	local platform_hub = {}
12	
13	local PREFIX = "mts_hub_widget_"
14	
15	local POSITIONS = {
16	    left   = defines.relative_gui_position.left,
17	    right  = defines.relative_gui_position.right,
18	    top    = defines.relative_gui_position.top,
19	    bottom = defines.relative_gui_position.bottom,
20	}
21	
22	-- How often (ticks) open hub widgets are refreshed. A space platform hub has
23	-- no "inventory changed" event, so to keep widgets live (clone added/removed,
24	-- platform arrived, base established) we re-raise the build event on a bounded
25	-- poll -- only for players who actually have a hub open.
26	local REFRESH_INTERVAL = 15
27	
28	--- Create-or-reuse the anchored frame for each registered widget and hand it to
29	--- the owning mod to (re)fill. The frame is REUSED across refreshes (not
30	--- destroyed), so a consumer that updates in place gets no flicker.
31	local function build_for(player, entity)
32	    for _, def in ipairs(remote_api.get_platform_hub_widgets()) do
33	        local name  = PREFIX .. def.name
34	        local frame = player.gui.relative[name]
35	        if not (frame and frame.valid) then
36	            frame = player.gui.relative.add{
37	                type      = "frame",
38	                name      = name,
39	                caption   = def.caption,
40	                direction = "vertical",
41	                anchor    = {
42	                    gui      = defines.relative_gui_type.space_platform_hub_gui,
43	                    position = POSITIONS[def.position] or defines.relative_gui_position.right,
44	                },
45	            }
46	            frame.style.padding = 8
47	        end
48	        script.raise_event(remote_api.events.on_platform_hub_gui_built, {
49	            player_index = player.index,
50	            widget_name  = def.name,
51	            element      = frame,
52	            entity       = entity,
53	        })
54	    end
55	end
56	
57	local function on_gui_opened(event)
58	    if event.gui_type ~= defines.gui_type.entity then return end
59	    local entity = event.entity
60	    if not (entity and entity.valid and entity.type == "space-platform-hub") then return end
61	    local player = game.get_player(event.player_index)
62	    if player and player.valid then build_for(player, entity) end
63	end
64	
65	--- Re-raise the build event for every player who currently has a hub open, so
66	--- widgets stay current. player.opened is synced game state, so this is
67	--- identical on every peer.
68	local function refresh_open(_)
69	    for _, player in pairs(game.connected_players) do
70	        local o = player.opened
71	        if o and o.object_name == "LuaEntity" and o.valid
72	           and o.type == "space-platform-hub" then
73	            build_for(player, o)
74	        end
75	    end
76	end
77	
78	function platform_hub.register()
79	    script.on_event(defines.events.on_gui_opened, on_gui_opened)
80	    script.on_nth_tick(REFRESH_INTERVAL, refresh_open)
81	end
82	
83	return platform_hub

112	--- Draw the research diff view comparing viewer_force against a target team.
113	--- @param content_frame  LuaGuiElement  scrollable pane to draw into
114	--- @param viewer_force   LuaForce
115	--- @param viewer_clock   number|nil     tick the viewer's team started
116	--- @param target_force_name string      internal force name (e.g. "team-1")
117	--- @param collapsed_cols number         number of icon columns per row
118	function research_diff.draw(content_frame, viewer_force, viewer_clock, target_force_name, collapsed_cols)
119	    -- Resolve target force
120	    local target_force = game.forces[target_force_name]
121	    if not target_force then
122	        content_frame.add{type = "label", caption = "Team '" .. target_force_name .. "' not found."}
123	        return
124	    end
125	
126	    -- Target clock start (team clock, not player clock)
127	    local target_clock = (storage.team_clock_start or {})[target_force_name]
128	
129	    -- Back button
130	    local back_btn = content_frame.add{
131	        type    = "button",
132	        name    = "sb_research_back",
133	        caption = "< Back",
134	        style   = "back_button",
135	    }
136	    back_btn.style.bottom_margin = 6
137	
138	    -- Context: who started earlier
139	    local target_owner = helpers.display_name(target_force_name)
140	    local viewer_owner = helpers.display_name(viewer_force.name)
141	    if viewer_clock and target_clock then
142	        local diff_ticks = math.abs(viewer_clock - target_clock)
143	        local context
144	        if viewer_clock < target_clock then
145	            context = "You started " .. research_diff.fmt_duration(diff_ticks) .. " earlier than " .. target_owner
146	        elseif target_clock < viewer_clock then
147	            context = target_owner .. " started " .. research_diff.fmt_duration(diff_ticks) .. " earlier than you"
148	        else
149	            context = "You both started at the same time"
150	        end
151	        local ctx_lbl = content_frame.add{type = "label", caption = context}
152	        ctx_lbl.style.font         = "default-bold"
153	        ctx_lbl.style.font_color   = {0.7, 0.9, 0.7}
154	        ctx_lbl.style.bottom_margin = 8
155	    end
156	
157	    -- Compute diff sets
158	    local viewer_ticks = research_diff.force_ticks(viewer_force)
159	    local target_ticks = research_diff.force_ticks(target_force)
160	
161	    -- both_have: researched by both
162	    local both_have = {}
163	    -- they_have: researched by target but NOT by viewer
164	    local they_have = {}
165	    -- you_have: researched by viewer but NOT by target
166	    local you_have  = {}
167	
168	    for name, tech in pairs(target_force.technologies) do
169	        if tech.researched then
170	            if viewer_force.technologies[name] and viewer_force.technologies[name].researched then
171	                both_have[#both_have + 1] = {
172	                    name      = name,
173	                    localised = helpers.tech_label(tech),
174	                    tick      = target_ticks[name],
175	                    order     = tech.order,
176	                }
177	            else
178	                they_have[#they_have + 1] = {
179	                    name      = name,
180	                    localised = helpers.tech_label(tech),
181	                    tick      = target_ticks[name],
182	                    order     = tech.order,
183	                }
184	            end
185	        end
186	    end
187	
188	    for name, tech in pairs(viewer_force.technologies) do
189	        if tech.researched and not (target_force.technologies[name] and target_force.technologies[name].researched) then
190	            you_have[#you_have + 1] = {
191	                name      = name,
192	                localised = helpers.tech_label(tech),
193	                tick      = viewer_ticks[name],
194	                order     = tech.order,
195	            }
196	        end
197	    end
198	
199	    -- Sort each set by timestamp (then tech.order for unstamped)
200	    local function sort_diff(list)
201	        local stamped, unstamped = {}, {}
202	        for _, e in ipairs(list) do
203	            if e.tick then stamped[#stamped+1] = e else unstamped[#unstamped+1] = e end
204	        end
205	        table.sort(stamped,   function(a, b) return a.tick  < b.tick  end)
206	        table.sort(unstamped, function(a, b) return a.order < b.order end)
207	        for _, v in ipairs(unstamped) do stamped[#stamped+1] = v end
208	        return stamped
209	    end
210	    both_have = sort_diff(both_have)
211	    they_have = sort_diff(they_have)
212	    you_have  = sort_diff(you_have)
213	
214	    local cols = collapsed_cols
215	
216	    local function diff_section(title, list, clock_for_tooltip)
217	        local hdr = content_frame.add{type = "label", caption = title .. "  (" .. #list .. ")"}
218	        hdr.style.font          = "default-bold"
219	        hdr.style.top_margin    = 6
220	        hdr.style.bottom_margin = 2
221	
222	        if #list == 0 then
223	            local none = content_frame.add{type = "label", caption = "(none)"}
224	            none.style.font_color = {0.5, 0.5, 0.5}
225	        else
226	            local grid = content_frame.add{type = "table", column_count = cols}
227	            grid.style.horizontal_spacing = 0
228	            grid.style.vertical_spacing   = 0
229	            research_diff.add_tech_icons(grid, list, clock_for_tooltip)
230	        end
231	    end
232	
233	    -- Use viewer's clock for shared techs tooltip (arbitrary choice; both valid)
234	    diff_section("You both have researched", both_have, viewer_clock)
235	    diff_section(target_owner .. " has, you don't", they_have, target_clock)
236	    diff_section("You have, " .. target_owner .. " doesn't", you_have, viewer_clock)
237	
238	    -- Infinite tech level differences
239	    local inf_diffs = {}
240	    for name, v_tech in pairs(viewer_force.technologies) do
241	        local t_tech = target_force.technologies[name]
242	        if v_tech.researched and t_tech and t_tech.researched then
243	            local vl = (v_tech.level  or 1)
244	            local tl = (t_tech.level  or 1)
245	            if vl ~= tl then
246	                inf_diffs[#inf_diffs + 1] = {
247	                    name   = name,
248	                    v_lvl  = vl,
249	                    t_lvl  = tl,
250	                    loc    = helpers.tech_label(v_tech),
251	                }
252	            end
253	        end
254	    end
255	
256	    if #inf_diffs > 0 then
257	        table.sort(inf_diffs, function(a, b)
258	            return tostring(a.name) < tostring(b.name)
259	        end)
260	        local hdr2 = content_frame.add{type = "label", caption = "Infinite tech level differences"}
261	        hdr2.style.font         = "default-bold"
262	        hdr2.style.top_margin   = 8
263	        hdr2.style.bottom_margin = 2
264	
265	        local inf_tbl = content_frame.add{type = "table", column_count = 3}
266	        inf_tbl.style.horizontal_spacing = 12
267	        inf_tbl.style.vertical_spacing   = 2
268	        -- Header row
269	        local function hd(txt)
270	            local l = inf_tbl.add{type = "label", caption = txt}
271	            l.style.font = "default-bold"
272	        end
273	        hd("Technology"); hd("You"); hd(target_owner)
274	        for _, d in ipairs(inf_diffs) do
275	            inf_tbl.add{type = "label", caption = d.loc}
276	            local vl = inf_tbl.add{type = "label", caption = "Lv " .. d.v_lvl}
277	            local tl = inf_tbl.add{type = "label", caption = "Lv " .. d.t_lvl}
278	            if d.v_lvl > d.t_lvl then
279	                vl.style.font_color = {0.4, 1, 0.4}
280	            else
281	                tl.style.font_color = {0.4, 1, 0.4}
282	            end
283	        end
284	    end
285	end
286	
287	return research_diff

Structural findings for the localisation plan: (1) nav.lua persists top-bar button specs INCLUDING the tooltip string into storage.nav_button_order and replays them via nav.rebuild_buttons — plain-English tooltips (e.g. research.lua:172 "Research Comparison") get frozen into save files; migrating to LocalisedString tooltips needs a storage migration and a check that a LocalisedString survives the storage round-trip. (2) helpers.add_title_bar(frame, title) is a shared pipeline taking a plain string title ("Landing Pen", "Ready to Start?", and the concatenated "Research: You vs X"); converting its signature to accept LocalisedString covers several call sites at once. (3) helpers.fmt_duration is the shared tick-to-time formatter used by research_diff/research_overview; its output is always embedded mid-sentence via '..' ("X playing", "Researched: X after spawn", "You started X earlier than ..."), so every consumer needs parameterised locale keys. (4) helpers.display_name/helpers.team_tag inject team/player names mid-sentence throughout pen_gui and research files — classic word-order hazard; team_tag likely contains rich-text. (5) research_diff tooltips already use LocalisedString {"", localised_label, hardcoded_suffix} form (status partial) — easiest migration, just replace the hardcoded tails with keyed parameters. (6) Repeated pattern of English variants chosen in Lua and/or expressions: pen_gui spawn-button 3-way tooltip (lines 171-175), leader "— offline" suffix, research_diff 3-way clock context, queue "Currently researching"/"Queued at position N", overview "Collapse"/"Expand all N technologies" — each variant must become its own locale key. (7) diff_section (research_diff.lua:216-217) appends "  (N)" to every passed section title — count formatting should move into the keys. (8) pen_info_panel writes display_panel_text, an API that accepts only a plain string shown identically to all players (and on the map); the default text plus admin-authored run descriptions cannot be per-player localised — document as a known limitation. (9) platform_hub frame captions come from other mods via remote_api.register_platform_hub_widget def.caption — pass-through, consumers own localisation. (10) start_playing_gui.lua:38 uses English possessive ("{team}'s clock") and hardcodes the "(press M)" keybind instead of a control-input locale reference. (11) research_diff.lua:257 sorts the infinite-tech table by internal prototype name while displaying localised labels — display order will look unsorted in other languages; research_overview.get_player_forces tie-breaks section order on the display name string. (12) helpers.diag (return_button.lua:75) is a debug message pipeline building plain strings; fine to leave unlocalised but worth a policy decision. Several helpers-owned strings (add_title_bar close button, add_show_offline_checkbox caption, team_tag, diag) live in scripts/helpers.lua, outside this file set — scan it next.
